title: 52-bit-VA gated Y-cluster joint-2X 7x37b birthday search on secp256k1 at 123.537334876573324 (per-generator i.i.d. X, MX=12)

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold gated grouped stored-leaf birthday search of proof.md on a 52-bit-VA generator/relay/home machine recovers x with unconditional single-run probability at least 0.3901 over the challenge and fresh algorithm coins. One coordinator first draws a 128-bit RNDR coin u and halts with no output unless u < K_GATE = 132919164825389149851328308155366463994 (p_gate = K_GATE/2^128 = 0.390614318; GATE = 256 instructions charged on every run); otherwise it runs q1 = 11,600,000,000 batches in G = 1536 power-law groups (m_g = floor(q1*(g/1536)^(28/32))) on 2^68 generators (2^58 clusters of 1024, each generator drawing MX=12 independent uniform permanent scalars), 2^42 relays and 2^84 homes (CAP_H = 164,136,470,183,936 records). The opened run succeeds with probability lo_run >= 0.998683334439 (Chen-Stein on the good-collision count, success.md 6.1-6.6), so p_gate * lo_run >= 0.39010001 >= 0.3901. Expected total work E_total = 256 + p_gate * E_run is at most 2^123.537334876573324 units of 1000 scalar AArch64 instructions (opened run E_run <= 2^124.893518 units, at most 76.4250 instructions per leaf of S = 2^128.603331). Peak memory at most 2^137.0002 bytes; opened-run preprocessing at most 2^117.0429 units, included in E_run; no advice. certificate.py checks the ledger, the 5.1 itemizations, the rate bounds and the census figures.

experiments.purpose: Checks yround Y-chain generation, the MX=12 7x37b/P1/LS64 leaf kernels against bit-exact models and affine addition, tbld-built table consumption and mutant rejections for all four table geometries (experiment.py, sites.py); the disjoint 52-bit-VA generator/relay/home + Y-ring machine, a registry address trace, completion and LS64/VA52/encoding mutant rejections (machine.py); the 128-bit gate and signed-VA R2 wraparound; toy-curve (p = 43, r = 31) checks of the Chen-Stein joint-term cases; and the kernel counts against certificate.py's constants.
